A16-7.label: Psychological Drama
A16-7.defn: A drama whose engine is one person's inner state of trauma, guilt or obsession, rendered from inside (Peppermint Candy, Affliction, Death in Venice, The Master). A drama of mourning goes to Grief Drama, one of madness and mental illness to Mental Illness Drama; where suspense drives it, see A3; where the crisis is existential rather than psychological, A16-8.
A16-7.axis: by the inner condition: trauma and abuse first, then guilt and atonement, and obsession last

new_leaves.label: Grief Drama
new_leaves.breadth: Dramas of mourning: the bereaved spouse, parent or friend living through a death
new_leaves.defn: A drama whose subject is grief itself — a widow, widower, parent or friend living through loss, often in the long aftermath of a death (Three Colors: Blue, Maborosi, Manchester by the Sea, Drive My Car). A family collectively bereaved goes to Family Drama; a grief that becomes breakdown, to Mental Illness Drama.

new_leaves.label: Mental Illness Drama
new_leaves.breadth: Dramas of madness, breakdown, psychosis and the asylum
new_leaves.defn: A drama of a mind coming apart — schizophrenia, psychosis, depression, dissociation, breakdown — or of life in the asylum and clinic (Through a Glass Darkly, The Cobweb, Clean, Shaven, Spider, Take Shelter). A psychological thriller goes to A3; a grief drama to Grief Drama.
new_leaves.aliases: madness film; asylum drama; mental illness in film
new_leaves.axis: by era: the studio-era psychiatric drama, the anti-psychiatry and modernist decades, then the contemporary independent character study

A16-4.label: Father–Child Drama
A16-4.defn: A drama centred on a father and his child — the father–son or father–daughter bond strained, broken or repaired, into the father's old age (The Return, Aftersun, Fences, On Golden Pond, Like Father, Like Son). A mother and child goes to Mother–Child Drama; a drama of the whole family to A16-3; Japanese shomingeki to A16-1.
A16-4.axis: by the child and the stage of life: fathers and sons, fathers and daughters, then ageing fathers (and parents) with their adult children

new_leaves.label: Mother–Child Drama
new_leaves.breadth: Dramas of a mother and her daughter or son
new_leaves.defn: A drama centred on a mother and her child — the mother–daughter or mother–son bond, from childhood to the mother's old age (Autumn Sonata, Terms of Endearment, Mommy, I Killed My Mother, Room). A father and child goes to Father–Child Drama; a drama of the whole family to A16-3.
new_leaves.axis: by the child and the stage of life: mothers and daughters, mothers and sons, then ageing mothers (and grandmothers) with their adult children

A20-7.label: Art Film
A20-7.defn: A narrative feature whose avant-garde form (tableau, recitation, fragmentation, dream logic, anti-illusion) is its defining element (A Page of Madness, Limit, The Color of Pomegranates, Russian Ark, Holy Motors). The political-modernist 'counter-cinema' of Duras, Straub–Huillet, Godard and Rainer goes to Counter-Cinema; films made by gallery artists or for installation to Artists' Film & Video Installation; duration-based art films to A1-39 Slow Cinema.
A20-7.axis: by era: the silent and interwar avant-garde feature, the poetic cinema of the 1960s–80s, then the later art-house avant-garde by period

new_leaves.label: Counter-Cinema
new_leaves.breadth: Political-modernist narrative features of the 1960s–80s that dismantle illusion: text, recitation, distanciation
new_leaves.defn: A narrative feature in the political-modernist tradition Peter Wollen named 'counter-cinema': estrangement over identification, text and recitation over drama, the soundtrack split from the image, the narrative opened to theory (India Song, From the Clouds to the Resistance, Riddles of the Sphinx, Film About a Woman Who..., Salomé). Its core is 1968–1990, with its auteurs' later work; dream and tableau art films without that programme stay in Art Film.
new_leaves.aliases: political modernism; cinéma de la modernité; Brechtian cinema
new_leaves.axis: by national tradition: France and Belgium; Italy, Iberia and Greece; the German-speaking and Central European wing; the Anglo-American feminist wing; the Third Cinema wing

new_leaves.label: Artists' Film & Video Installation
new_leaves.breadth: Narrative and quasi-narrative works by gallery artists, and moving-image installations
new_leaves.defn: A moving-image work made by a visual artist from the gallery world, shown as a feature, a cycle or a multi-screen installation (Cremaster 3, Rape, Manifesto, Inconsolable Memories, Primitive). Underground and experimental filmmakers outside the art world stay in Art Film or their own leaves.
new_leaves.aliases: artists' cinema; gallery film; moving-image installation
new_leaves.axis: by form and period: installations and exhibitions, then artists' features before and after 2010
